improvement projects"}],"title":{"type":"text","$t":"QI PROJECT- IMPROVING POST-GRADUATE RESEARCH PROJECTS"},"content":{"type":"html","$t":"\u003Cp\u003EWe, from the Department of General Medicine, at Kamineni Institute of Medical Sciences made high-quality research our top priority. Research within the field of General Medicine is crucial for advancing medical knowledge, improving patient outcomes, and implementing evidence-based medicine in practice. In our department, several research projects are currently underway, addressing a wide range of clinical issues. However, the effectiveness and efficiency of ongoing research projects can be significantly influenced by organizational and procedural frameworks within a department. Despite the commitment to high-quality research, various challenges have been identified that may hinder the successful completion and impact of these projects. The main challenge was insufficient research knowledge among post-graduates conducting the research. Their research needs improvements in terms of organizing the collected data and defining objectives and methodology to initiate with. Further improvements to obtain efficient results from the data available, and draw conclusions from the results obtained.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EOur QIP (Quality improvement project) is based on the PDSA (Plan-Do-Study-Act) methodology.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cb\u003EWhat conditions indicated the need for the project?\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E-The inability of post-graduates to conduct an efficient research.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E-Lack of research knowledge among post-graduates leading to an overall decrease in the research quality of the department.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E-Problems with the validation of data collection\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E-Inability of post-graduates to formulate results from the data available.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E-Questionable generalizability of the research projects\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cb\u003EAIM OF THE QI PROJECT:\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThis QI project aims to bridge the knowledge gaps in research, among post-graduate students and improve the quality of the research conducted by them.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThis project also aims to enhance the research quality of the department.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cb\u003EOBJECTIVES\u003C\/b\u003E:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ETo include a relevant introduction in the thesis projects\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ETo help post-graduates conduct an effective review of the literature\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ETo improve the stated methodology\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ETo assess and improve the observations and results of the research project\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ETo assess if the stated aims and objectives are met correctly by the end of the research\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ETo train the researchers to obtain valid conclusions from the results obtained\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cb\u003EIs it SMART\u003C\/b\u003E: Single-focused, measurable, action-oriented, realistic, and timely?\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EYes, our goals are single-focused (improving research quality), measurable (number of research parameters showing improved quality against a set standard), action-oriented (Improved research quality over time with regular QI cycles), realistic (deals with our everyday workflow), and timely (analysis of the research projects will be done as soon as they are discussed with us).\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cb\u003EWhat is the problem?\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E1. Characterize the problem\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E2. What causes are explored\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cb\u003EHow do you know it is a problem?\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThe baseline will be measured against a set standard.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAnalysis of research projects conducted by post-graduates shows none or very few have reached the set standards. Some apparent problems were:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E-Incomplete research projects\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E-Improperly stated methodology due to lack of knowledge on how to describe the methodology\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E-No or very minimal discussion in the form of comparison with other studies or review of literature is done.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E-The table headings in the results are not clearly stated\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E-Poor correlation between the stated aims and objectives and the results obtained through the tables in these research projects\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E-No stated conclusions available\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cb\u003EWhat is the solution?\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E-Does it cover short and long term?\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E-Does in consider up and downstream?\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cb\u003EWhat is the plan for successful implementation?\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E-How will I set a target?\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E-How often will progress be measured?\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPredictions:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E-What do we expect to see and why?\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E-What consequences may be there?\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E-Could the change make something worse?\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp;By the time this QI project is being conducted, data collection is completed by post-graduates. So, data validation remains the main issue in moving forward. However, post-graduates were able to provide case report links, case sheets, collected images, and written case report forms with in-patient numbers on them to prove the validity and accuracy of data entries.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u0026nbsp;RESEARCH PROJECTS CONSIDERED FOR THIS QI PROJECT:\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EDr.NARSIMHA : PREDICTORS OF OUTCOMES IN PATIENTS WITH COMPLEX DIABETES\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EDr. PAVAN KUMAR : MANAGING SARCOPENIA AND VISCERAL FAT DRIVEN VASCULAR OUTCOMES IN PATIENTS WITH DIABETES\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EDr.DEEPIKA: CLINICAL AND RADIOLOGICAL PROFILE, RISK FACTORS MANAGEMENT AND OUTCOMES IN CASES OF ACUTE STROKE\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EDr. HARI PRIYA: RISK FACTORS, CLINICAL SPECTRUM, DIAGNOSTIC AND OUTCOME PREDICTORS OF PATIENTS WITH ENCEPHALOPATHY\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EDr. BHARATH: OUTCOMES OF MONITORING ACUTE AND CHRONIC GLOMERULAR INJURIES WITH SPOT AND 24 HOUR URINARY PROTEIN CREATININE ESTIMATION\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EDr.NISHITHA: RESOLVING DIAGNOSTIC AND THERAPEUTIC UNCERTAINTIES AND IMPROVING OUTCOMES IN PATIENTS WITH UNDIFFERENTIATED FEVER\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EDr.KEERTHI: DIAGNOSTIC AND THERAPEUTIC UNCERTAINTIES IN TB\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EDr.PAVANI: CLINICAL COMPLEXITIES IN MANAGMENT AND OUTCOMES OF PATIENTS WITH SIGNIFICANT ANEMIA\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EDr.VENKAT SAI: ETIOLOGY AND OUTCOMES IN PATIENTS WITH SUSPECTED CLD\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EDr.KRANTHI: THERAPEUTIC OUTCOMES IN PATIENTS WITH CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASES IN CKD\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E*Scoring systems for the research projects:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both; text-align: center;\"\u003E\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/blogger.googleusercontent.com\/img\/b\/R29vZ2xl\/AVvXsEiH2Si0R6BoNGAkCXOmYn52pO5-p1KfRbFIWqXG1wqYvI2CUBKSFUME654fuKpF5FIQg0cDKoNeJor9olcecawrrp20zzeYHvzGUnQUkmpCw_uUjt1jPAGMI6R8NkxOLeCOXTmsHqvqQiT-ilZNeFhZqB9nvUvZQh_lPmmQ7Ju53Qo3DJq6A3Ebg3Ti8nO0\/s1544\/3CE8EA6A-CD4D-4C07-8BFD-F3ACD39E2065.jpeg\" imageanchor=\"1\" style=\"margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;\"\u003E\u003Cimg border=\"0\" data-original-height=\"1170\" data-original-width=\"1544\" height=\"242\" src=\"https:\/\/blogger.googleusercontent.com\/img\/b\/R29vZ2xl\/AVvXsEiH2Si0R6BoNGAkCXOmYn52pO5-p1KfRbFIWqXG1wqYvI2CUBKSFUME654fuKpF5FIQg0cDKoNeJor9olcecawrrp20zzeYHvzGUnQUkmpCw_uUjt1jPAGMI6R8NkxOLeCOXTmsHqvqQiT-ilZNeFhZqB9nvUvZQh_lPmmQ7Ju53Qo3DJq6A3Ebg3Ti8nO0\/s320\/3CE8EA6A-CD4D-4C07-8BFD-F3ACD39E2065.jpeg\" width=\"320\" \/\u003E\u003C\/a\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both; text-align: center;\"\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cu\u003ESET STANDARDS FOR COMPARISON:\u003C\/u\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cb\u003EDOMAIN -1:\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/b\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: UICTFontTextStyleBody; font-size: 17px;\"\u003E\u003Cb\u003EDocumentation of Data Collected:\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p1\" style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: auto; font-size: 17px; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal; margin: 0px; text-size-adjust: auto;\"\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"s1\" style=\"font-family: UICTFontTextStyleBody;\"\u003E\u003Cb\u003EComponents:\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p1\" style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: auto; font-size: 17px; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal; margin: 0px; text-size-adjust: auto;\"\u003EThe domain \"Documentation of Data Collected\" assesses how well data are recorded and documented on case report forms and master charts. Here are the components of this domain:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p1\" style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: auto; font-size: 17px; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal; margin: 0px; text-size-adjust: auto;\"\u003E1. Completeness of Data Entries:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p1\" style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: auto; font-size: 17px; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal; margin: 0px; text-size-adjust: auto;\"\u003E\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp;- Whether all required data fields are filled out on the case report forms and master charts is evaluated as incomplete entries can hinder the accuracy and reliability of the data.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p1\" style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: auto; font-size: 17px; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal; margin: 0px; text-size-adjust: auto;\"\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p1\" style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: auto; font-size: 17px; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal; margin: 0px; text-size-adjust: auto;\"\u003E2. Clarity and Legibility:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p1\" style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: auto; font-size: 17px; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal; margin: 0px; text-size-adjust: auto;\"\u003E\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp;- The clarity and legibility of the handwriting or documentation on the case report forms and master charts are assessed. Clear and legible documentation is essential for accurate interpretation and analysis of the data.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p1\" style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: auto; font-size: 17px; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal; margin: 0px; text-size-adjust: auto;\"\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p1\" style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: auto; font-size: 17px; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal; margin: 0px; text-size-adjust: auto;\"\u003E3. Consistency Between Forms:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p1\" style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: auto; font-size: 17px; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal; margin: 0px; text-size-adjust: auto;\"\u003E\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp;- Checking for consistency between the data recorded on the case report forms and master charts. Consistency ensures reliability and coherence in the dataset.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p1\" style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: auto; font-size: 17px; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal; margin: 0px; text-size-adjust: auto;\"\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p1\" style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: auto; font-size: 17px; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal; margin: 0px; text-size-adjust: auto;\"\u003E4. Timeliness of Data Recording:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p1\" style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: auto; font-size: 17px; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal; margin: 0px; text-size-adjust: auto;\"\u003E\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp;- Consider the timeliness of data recording on the case report forms and master charts. Timely documentation prevents delays and ensures the availability of up-to-date data for analysis.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p1\" style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: auto; font-size: 17px; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal; margin: 0px; text-size-adjust: auto;\"\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p1\" style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: auto; font-size: 17px; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal; margin: 0px; text-size-adjust: auto;\"\u003E5. Documentation of Exceptions or Deviations:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p1\" style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: auto; font-size: 17px; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal; margin: 0px; text-size-adjust: auto;\"\u003E\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp;- Assess whether any exceptions or deviations from the standard data collection procedures are documented appropriately on the case report forms and master charts. Documenting exceptions helps maintain transparency and integrity in the data.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p1\" style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: auto; font-size: 17px; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal; margin: 0px; text-size-adjust: auto;\"\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p1\" style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: auto; font-size: 17px; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal; margin: 0px; text-size-adjust: auto;\"\u003E6. Organization of Data Entries:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p1\" style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: auto; font-size: 17px; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal; margin: 0px; text-size-adjust: auto;\"\u003E\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp;- Evaluate the organization and structure of data entries on the case report forms and master charts. Well-organized data entries facilitate easy retrieval and analysis of the data.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p1\" style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: auto; font-size: 17px; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal; margin: 0px; text-size-adjust: auto;\"\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p1\" style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: auto; font-size: 17px; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal; margin: 0px; text-size-adjust: auto;\"\u003E7. Cross-Referencing and Verification:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p1\" style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: auto; font-size: 17px; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal; margin: 0px; text-size-adjust: auto;\"\u003E\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp;- Check if there are mechanisms in place for cross-referencing and verifying the data recorded on the case report forms and master charts. Cross-referencing ensures accuracy and reliability by detecting discrepancies or errors.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p1\" style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: auto; font-size: 17px; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal; margin: 0px; text-size-adjust: auto;\"\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p1\" style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: auto; font-size: 17px; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal; margin: 0px; text-size-adjust: auto;\"\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"s1\" style=\"font-family: UICTFontTextStyleBody;\"\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p1\" style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: auto; font-size: 17px; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal; margin: 0px; text-size-adjust: auto;\"\u003EBy assessing these components, we can determine the quality and reliability of the data documentation process in the research project.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p1\" style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: auto; font-size: 17px; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal; margin: 0px; text-size-adjust: auto;\"\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p1\" style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: auto; font-size: 17px; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal; margin: 0px; text-size-adjust: auto;\"\u003E\u003Cb\u003EDetermination of score for domain-1 to quantify the quality:\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p1\" style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: auto; font-size: 17px; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal; margin: 0px; text-size-adjust: auto;\"\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"s1\" style=\"font-family: UICTFontTextStyleBody;\"\u003EPoor (1):\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p1\" style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: auto; font-size: 17px; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal; margin: 0px; text-size-adjust: auto;\"\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"s1\" style=\"font-family: UICTFontTextStyleBody;\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003Cspan class=\"Apple-converted-space\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E- Incomplete or missing data entries on case report forms and master charts.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p1\" style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: auto; font-size: 17px; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal; margin: 0px; text-size-adjust: auto;\"\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"s1\" style=\"font-family: UICTFontTextStyleBody;\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003Cspan class=\"Apple-converted-space\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E- Lack of clarity in handwriting or documentation, making it difficult to interpret the data.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p1\" style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: auto; font-size: 17px; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal; margin: 0px; text-size-adjust: auto;\"\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"s1\" style=\"font-family: UICTFontTextStyleBody;\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003Cspan class=\"Apple-converted-space\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E- Significant discrepancies between data recorded on case report forms and master charts.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p2\" style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: auto; font-size: 17px; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal; margin: 0px; min-height: 26.8px; text-size-adjust: auto;\"\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"s1\" style=\"font-family: UICTFontTextStyleBody;\"\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p1\" style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: auto; font-size: 17px; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal; margin: 0px; text-size-adjust: auto;\"\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"s1\" style=\"font-family: UICTFontTextStyleBody;\"\u003EFair (2):\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p1\" style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: auto; BlinkMacSystemFont, \u0026quot;Segoe UI (Custom)\u0026quot;, Roboto, \u0026quot;Helvetica Neue\u0026quot;, \u0026quot;Open Sans (Custom)\u0026quot;, system-ui, -apple-system, \u0026quot;Segoe UI\u0026quot;, Roboto, Ubuntu, Cantarell, \u0026quot;Noto Sans\u0026quot;, sans-serif, \u0026quot;Apple Color Emoji\u0026quot;, \u0026quot;Segoe UI Emoji\u0026quot;\" style=\"background-color: white; color: #121512; font-size: 16px; white-space-collapse: preserve;\"\u003EA 47-year-old male, known to be diabetic, presented with fever, severe weight loss, and loss of appetite for one month. He has a previous history of pulmonary tuberculosis seven years ago, for which he underwent Anti-Tuberculosis Treatment (ATT) for six months. He also reported experiencing loose stools for the past ten days. Additionally, he complained of passing small amounts of stools during urination and weakness in all four limbs. Physical examination revealed normal vital signs, bronchovesicular breath sounds in both lung apices, and a non-tender soft abdomen. The neurological examination was found to be normal.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"background-color: white; box-sizing: border-box; color: #121512; font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, \u0026quot;Segoe UI (Custom)\u0026quot;, Roboto, \u0026quot;Helvetica Neue\u0026quot;, \u0026quot;Open Sans (Custom)\u0026quot;, system-ui, -apple-system, \u0026quot;Segoe UI\u0026quot;, Roboto, Ubuntu, Cantarell, \u0026quot;Noto Sans\u0026quot;, sans-serif, \u0026quot;Apple Color Emoji\u0026quot;, \u0026quot;Segoe UI Emoji\u0026quot;; font-size: 16px; margin: 1.25em 0px; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space-collapse: preserve;\"\u003EHe had received treatment at other hospitals with antibiotics, but there was no improvement in the fever which persisted. The differential diagnoses considered included reactivation of pulmonary tuberculosis and Pott's spine (suggested by weakness and fecal incontinence). Further investigations revealed anemia, elevated ESR, and a creatinine level of 2.1 (renal TB was suspected). Fever profiles, including tests for dengue and malaria smears, were negative.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"background-color: white; box-sizing: border-box; color: #121512; font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, \u0026quot;Segoe UI (Custom)\u0026quot;, Roboto, \u0026quot;Helvetica Neue\u0026quot;, \u0026quot;Open Sans (Custom)\u0026quot;, system-ui, -apple-system, \u0026quot;Segoe UI\u0026quot;, Roboto, Ubuntu, Cantarell, \u0026quot;Noto Sans\u0026quot;, sans-serif, \u0026quot;Apple Color Emoji\u0026quot;, \u0026quot;Segoe UI Emoji\u0026quot;; font-size: 16px; margin: 1.25em 0px; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space-collapse: preserve;\"\u003EDuring hospital rounds, questions were raised regarding the potential causes of fecal incontinence. Rectal TB was considered as a differential diagnosis, and the role of proctoscopy in the evaluation of rectal TB was discussed due to the unavailability of colonoscopy or sigmoidoscopy. Spinal TB was also considered, prompting an examination of sacral sensations and anal tone.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"background-color: white; box-sizing: border-box; color: #121512; font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, \u0026quot;Segoe UI (Custom)\u0026quot;, Roboto, \u0026quot;Helvetica Neue\u0026quot;, \u0026quot;Open Sans (Custom)\u0026quot;, system-ui, -apple-system, \u0026quot;Segoe UI\u0026quot;, Roboto, Ubuntu, Cantarell, \u0026quot;Noto Sans\u0026quot;, sans-serif, \u0026quot;Apple Color Emoji\u0026quot;, \u0026quot;Segoe UI Emoji\u0026quot;; font-size: 16px; margin: 1.25em 0px; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space-collapse: preserve;\"\u003EThe localization of fever was further investigated. Chest X-ray showed bilateral opacities and fibrotic changes as sequelae of previous infection, along with an enlarged right hilar lymph node. Blood and urine cultures were negative, and stool analysis was sent for evaluation. Despite not producing sputum, a referral to a pulmonologist was made, and a High-Resolution CT (HRCT) of the chest was planned.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"background-color: white; box-sizing: border-box; color: #121512; font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, \u0026quot;Segoe UI (Custom)\u0026quot;, Roboto, \u0026quot;Helvetica Neue\u0026quot;, \u0026quot;Open Sans (Custom)\u0026quot;, system-ui, -apple-system, \u0026quot;Segoe UI\u0026quot;, Roboto, Ubuntu, Cantarell, \u0026quot;Noto Sans\u0026quot;, sans-serif, \u0026quot;Apple Color Emoji\u0026quot;, \u0026quot;Segoe UI Emoji\u0026quot;; font-size: 16px; margin: 1.25em 0px; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space-collapse: preserve;\"\u003EReferrals were also made to a gastroenterologist due to concerns of disseminated TB. Investigations including a CT abdomen with oral contrast and colonoscopy were advised to rule out malignancy and intestinal TB given the patient's inconsistent history of melena, weight loss, and other symptoms.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"background-color: white; box-sizing: border-box; color: #121512; font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, \u0026quot;Segoe UI (Custom)\u0026quot;, Roboto, \u0026quot;Helvetica Neue\u0026quot;, \u0026quot;Open Sans (Custom)\u0026quot;, system-ui, -apple-system, \u0026quot;Segoe UI\u0026quot;, Roboto, Ubuntu, Cantarell, \u0026quot;Noto Sans\u0026quot;, sans-serif, \u0026quot;Apple Color Emoji\u0026quot;, \u0026quot;Segoe UI Emoji\u0026quot;; font-size: 16px; margin: 1.25em 0px; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space-collapse: preserve;\"\u003EFurther imaging revealed left upper lobe cavities and bronchiectasis with patchy consolidations on HRCT of the chest, along with findings of a paravertebral collection from C4-D1 vertebral bodies, chronic pancreatitis, and a right renal space-occupying lesion incidentally detected. Subsequent bronchoscopy confirmed the presence of Mycobacterium tuberculosis with Rifampicin sensitivity (TrueNAAT positive).\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"background-color: white; box-sizing: border-box; color: #121512; font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, \u0026quot;Segoe UI (Custom)\u0026quot;, Roboto, \u0026quot;Helvetica Neue\u0026quot;, \u0026quot;Open Sans (Custom)\u0026quot;, system-ui, -apple-system, \u0026quot;Segoe UI\u0026quot;, Roboto, Ubuntu, Cantarell, \u0026quot;Noto Sans\u0026quot;, sans-serif, \u0026quot;Apple Color Emoji\u0026quot;, \u0026quot;Segoe UI Emoji\u0026quot;; font-size: 16px; margin: 1.25em 0px 0px; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space-collapse: preserve;\"\u003EAn MRI of the cervical spine confirmed the diagnosis of Pott's spine. Anti-Tuberculosis Treatment (ATT) was initiated; however, the patient developed acute shortness of breath after returning home and required intubation. Unfortunately, the patient passed away later on, with the renal mass remaining uninvestigated\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p2\" style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: auto; font-size: 17px; font-stretch: normal; font-size: 17px; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal; margin: 0px; text-size-adjust: auto;\"\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"s1\" style=\"font-family: UICTFontTextStyleBody;\"\u003EPatient was resistant to 3 cycles of cyclophosphamide with steroid pulse and was not affordable for rituximab\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p1\" style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: auto; font-size: 17px; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal; margin: 0px; text-size-adjust: auto;\"\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"s1\" style=\"font-family: UICTFontTextStyleBody;\"\u003EHe was initiated on mycophenolate mofetil and is kept under follow up.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p2\" style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: auto; font-size: 17px; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal; margin: 0px; min-height: 26.8px; text-size-adjust: auto;\"\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"s1\" style=\"font-family: UICTFontTextStyleBody;\"\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p1\" style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: auto; font-size: 17px; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal; margin: 0px; text-size-adjust: auto;\"\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"s1\" style=\"font-family: UICTFontTextStyleBody;\"\u003E—————\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p1\" style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: auto; font-size: 17px; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal; margin: 0px; text-size-adjust: auto;\"\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"s1\" style=\"font-family: UICTFontTextStyleBody;\"\u003EReferral from psychiatry:\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p1\" style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: auto; font-size: 17px; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal; margin: 0px; text-size-adjust: auto;\"\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"s1\" style=\"font-family: UICTFontTextStyleBody;\"\u003EThe patient is a 36 year old male who was last seen by his wife in August 2023, after which he went to work as a lorry driver and went missing. The police could not find him. He traveled to many places in India (including Kasi) with some sadhus and ended up begging for food from his neighbor’s house in May 2024. He was seen by his in-laws and taken home.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p2\" style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: auto; font-size: 17px; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal; margin: 0px; min-height: 26.8px; text-size-adjust: auto;\"\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"s1\" style=\"font-family: UICTFontTextStyleBody;\"\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p1\" style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: auto; font-size: 17px; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal; margin: 0px; text-size-adjust: auto;\"\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"s1\" style=\"font-family: UICTFontTextStyleBody;\"\u003EThe patient reports complete retrograde amnesia. He does not remember anything from childhood to October 2023, until he woke up lying in a train in Bhubaneswar without knowing how he got there.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p1\" style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: auto; font-size: 17px; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal; margin: 0px; text-size-adjust: auto;\"\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"s1\" style=\"font-family: UICTFontTextStyleBody;\"\u003EImportantly, he is a chronic alcoholic.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p1\" style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: auto; font-size: 17px; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal; margin: 0px; text-size-adjust: auto;\"\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"s1\" style=\"font-family: UICTFontTextStyleBody;\"\u003EHe is not able to recall anything about his childhood or family, even if he is shown some photographs taken in the past\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p2\" style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: auto; font-size: 17px; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal; margin: 0px; min-height: 26.8px; text-size-adjust: auto;\"\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"s1\" style=\"font-family: UICTFontTextStyleBody;\"\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p1\" style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: auto; font-size: 17px; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal; margin: 0px; text-size-adjust: auto;\"\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"s1\" style=\"font-family: UICTFontTextStyleBody;\"\u003EChronic retrograde amnesia secondary to thiamine deficiency was suspected.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p1\" style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: auto; font-size: 17px; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal; margin: 0px; text-size-adjust: auto;\"\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"s1\" style=\"font-family: UICTFontTextStyleBody;\"\u003E---------------------------------\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p1\" style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: auto; font-size: 17px; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal; margin: 0px; text-size-adjust: auto;\"\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"s1\" style=\"font-family: UICTFontTextStyleBody;\"\u003EAdmissions on 28\/05\/2024\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p1\" style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: auto; font-size: 17px; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal; margin: 0px; text-size-adjust: auto;\"\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p1\" style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: auto; font-size: 17px; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal; margin: 0px; text-size-adjust: auto;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: UICTFontTextStyleBody;\"\u003E1.60 year old female patient with hypertension presented to the OPD with sudden onset bilateral drooping of eye lids for the last 2 days , and the examination revealed bilateral complete ptosis with loss of adduction, superior and inferior eye movements in both eyes with divergent squint, down and out eye on right side with dilated fixed pupils on both sides. Bilateral acute onset 3rd nerve palsy was suspected and the differentials considered were:\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p1\" style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: auto; font-size: 17px; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal; margin: 0px; text-size-adjust: auto;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: UICTFontTextStyleBody;\"\u003Ea. Midbrain stroke, b. Basilar artery thrombosis, c. Space occupying lesion in mid brain,\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p1\" style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: auto; font-size: 17px; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal; margin: 0px; text-size-adjust: auto;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: UICTFontTextStyleBody;\"\u003Ed. Miller-fischer-varient of GBS\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p1\" style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: auto; font-size: 17px; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal; margin: 0px; text-size-adjust: auto;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: UICTFontTextStyleBody;\"\u003EComplete neurological examination and MRI brain was done which revealed a hyperacute mid brain infarct\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p1\" style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: auto; font-size: 17px; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal; margin: 0px; text-size-adjust: auto;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: UICTFontTextStyleBody;\"\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p1\" style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: auto; font-size: 17px; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal; margin: 0px; text-size-adjust: auto;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: UICTFontTextStyleBody;\"\u003E2.A 53 year male presented with low grade fever for the last 2 months and high grade fever for 10 days. He was eventually diagnosed with chronic pancreatitis, pyelonephritis. The patient was managed with IV fluids maintaining adequate hydration and antibiotics. Urine and blood cultures were sent and CECT abdomen was planned\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p1\" style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: auto; font-size: 17px; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal; margin: 0px; text-size-adjust: auto;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: UICTFontTextStyleBody;\"\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p1\" style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: auto; font-size: 17px; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal; margin: 0px; text-size-adjust: auto;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: UICTFontTextStyleBody;\"\u003E3.A 50 year female presented to the ER with excessive tiredness and body pains. On examination she had pallor and she was febrile. Her hemogram revealed pancytopenia with retic count suggestive of hypo-proliferative marrow. Peripheral smear was showing evidence of dimorphic anemia but her serum ferritin and B12 levels were within normal limits. The patient is planned for bone marrow biopsy.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p1\" style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: auto; font-size: 17px; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal; margin: 0px; text-size-adjust: auto;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: UICTFontTextStyleBody;\"\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p1\" style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: auto; font-size: 17px; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal; margin: 0px; text-size-adjust: auto;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: UICTFontTextStyleBody;\"\u003E4.A 26 year female with history of hypothyroidism and membranous nephropathy admitted with uncontrolled sugars (? steroid induced ?tacrolimus induced ). The patient after being diagnosed with membranous nephropathy used steroids but as she developed cushingoid features steroids were gradually tapered and stopped 15 days ago. She was also started on Tab. Tacrolimus, 30 days\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: UICTFontTextStyleBody;\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;ago. On examination her abdominal striae appeared to have decreased compared to previous admission, however she has persistent pedal oedema. Her GRBS was HIGH and HbA1c was 8.1 and was switched to insulin mixtard. The possibility of steroid induced diabetes and tacrolimus induced hyperglycemia were considered.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p1\" style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: auto; font-size: 17px; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal; margin: 0px; text-size-adjust: auto;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: UICTFontTextStyleBody;\"\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p1\" style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: auto; font-size: 17px; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal; margin: 0px; text-size-adjust: auto;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: UICTFontTextStyleBody;\"\u003E5. A 60 year male with previous history of cerebrovascular attacks and medication incompliance, presented with sudden onset weakness of right upper and lower limb weakness for 1 day and diagnosed with acute infarct in left MCA territory. He was managed conservatively with anti-platelets and physiotherapy. After 1 day there improvement in the grade of power by 1 point.(3\/5 to 4\/5)\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p1\" style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: auto; font-size: 17px; font-stretch: normal; text-align: center;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"text-align: left;\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;Teaching course-\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp;“\u003Cb\u003ECLINICAL NEUROLOGY”\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp;“THEORY TO PRACTICE\u003C\/b\u003E”\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EA well-organized teaching course in neurology was designed by me with the help of my fellow senior residents (Dr. Shashikala, Dr. Manasa, Dr. Pradeep, Dr. Vamshi, Dr. Manoj, Dr. Gouthami) with the support of our beloved HOD, Dr. Rakesh Biswas.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThe main aim of this teaching course is to create interest among postgraduates in learning and teaching aspects of neurology. I planned to teach them on how to convert theoretical knowledge in neurology into practice.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EI organized the course in such a way that each theory\/seminar topic is followed by a relevant case presentation and journal. Postgraduates are trained in the theoretical aspects of the topic in the first class, and in the second class, the main focus is on examination techniques, making differential diagnoses, how to order appropriate investigations, and discussions on the management plan. Attendance to these sessions is monitored.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EEach seminar will be followed by a short 'best of four MCQ' exam to check the level of understanding of post-graduates and also to generate a competitive spirit among the students.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EDuring the seminar presentations as a course mentor, i go through the presentation of the post-graduate a day before and make necessary changes. As the presentation goes on, i try to simplify few complex concepts. I also check understanding among listeners from time to time.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EDuring case presentations, the post-graduate presenting the case will be assessed for his\/her history taking and examination skills. This will be followed by a discussion on investigations and formulating management plan.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both; text-align: center;\"\u003E\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/blogger.googleusercontent.com\/img\/b\/R29vZ2xl\/AVvXsEhg_WmzEzVB3D4xni6gBBW31Na0gAHmwTC2MzrhDT7gVLFuAqCHR7ffPtyn-tocSLZIyPOTSkXAInUqRiOutuypO_ZOM4pAgQpWvzunIcfmPWdkCQp0O0VLC2o_OZrnUr-Q793GC_0Q5SkaURWGhL7KJcUVklOu4ng3JeVypXFcqjpojiXkNUbmCDz2cVXK\/s4000\/3D5DB783-2C5A-46B1-BDCD-AD854FA26EFD.jpeg\" style=\"margin-left: 1em; text-align: center;\"\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAll the post-graduates were asked to come prepared with the topic, at-least the basic aspects.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ETOPIC- Arterial supply of brain and localization of stroke\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPRESENTOR-Dr.Prachetan\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EMODERATOR-Dr.Chandana\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E19 post-graduate students have attended the seminar\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cb\u003EArterial supply was discussed under the following headings-\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPosterior circulation\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ETerritorial supply of brain(Lateral surface, medial surface, undersurface)\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAnatomical course and branches of ICA,MCA,ACA,Circle of willis, PCA, Vertebro-basilar system.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cb\u003ELocalization of stroke was discussed under the following headings-\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EICA occlusion (Importance of ophthalmic artery,Angle brow and cheek pulsations, retinal changes)\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EACA stroke- mechanism of mono-paresis based on motor homonculus and a brief discussion on mechanism of transcortical aphasias.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EMCA stroke-Stem occulsion, M1 syndrome,M2 syndromes were dealt in detail with some example clinical scenarios given by me. Difference in clinical manifestations of involvement of dominant vs non-dominant hemisphere was explained.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EDominant-Language dysfunction, apraxias and angular gyrus(Grestmann syndrome),mechanism of alexia with agraphia was explained\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ENon dominant- Visuospatial neglect (explained with examples), dressing and constructional apraxias, emotional disturbances and delirium.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPCA strokes have been dealt in detail as P1 and P2 syndromes\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EP1- Dejerine-roussy syndrome,Thalamic syndromes\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EP2- Mechanism of various clinical manifestations have been dealt in detail such as-Visual agnosias, optic ataxia, balints syndrome, antons syndrome, asimultagnosia, pallinopsia, medial temporal lesions. Mechanism of alexia without agraphia was also explained by me.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EBrain stem syndromes- Various named brain stem syndromes have been introduced and few of them were dealt in detail (Ventral mid brain syndromes, Millard gubler syndrome and lateral medullary syndrome).\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EA “best of four MCQ” exam was conducted after the session.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E*\u003Cb\u003ESeminar 1 exam results 👏\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E*Highest score: 8\/10*\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EShiva kumar\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ESree teja\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAjay\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EGovardhini\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ENavya\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPrachetan\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E*2nd highest: 7\/10*\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EHimaja\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EVivek\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EDeepika\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EKranthi\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EVenkat sai\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EHari priya\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ENarsimha\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EOther post-graduates scored less than 7 were personally enquired about the problems and feedback was taken to improve the teaching sessions.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EASSESSMENT RESULTS OF FIRST YEAR POST-GRADUATES\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both; margin-right: 1em;\"\u003E\u003Cimg border=\"0\" data-original-height=\"1173\" data-original-width=\"1169\" height=\"320\" src=\"https:\/\/blogger.googleusercontent.com\/img\/b\/R29vZ2xl\/AVvXsEiGrquEeL1-bEx4UkuQT_GMADTeK-AkAPrEltOGAVzLSkA8ia3OoSO0TU3UPKHE7CkoW4VIhE8oysdQwSbc7KvFqcx8buVqkP2PCH45l0ehu3OsCLuEDdTCuWRkTgdc3hrBiPvmgzqnWS75jByUxPighFBPjTX2gTZybiROQx9tHFWv7THXYg99IQqdVNmJ\/s320\/F5602C47-E02C-4B32-BEEB-96635FFBF256.jpeg\" width=\"319\" \/\u003E\u003C\/a\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003Cp\u003EApart from session related feedbacks 2 interesting anonymous negative feedbacks have been found. Those feedbacks were related to the amount of stress he\/she is facing when he\/she has to manage the patient care, night duties and academics all together. As a result the academics seemed to be overburdening for them. My Plan is to address these concerns individually with counselling on how to manage the stress.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EReassurance was given in the 2nd session and a stress free and friendly environment rather than a formal teaching was promised to my students as far as my teaching sessions were concerned. I tried to engage each and every student in the room during the session. This change increased the amount of collective learning that has happened in the 2nd session and also few post-graduates asked doubts after the session which did not happen in the first session. Importance of creating a student friendly environment during the teaching sessions was the ultimate learning point for me.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"color: #cc0000;\"\u003ECASE PRESENTATION\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cb\u003EPresenter: Dr.Shiva Nagendra.\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cb\u003EModerator: Dr.Chandana\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EA total of 15 post-graduates attended the session.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E69 year old female presented with sudden onset weakness of left upper and lower limb for 6 days with acute infarct in right fronto-parietal region with multiple hypertensive micro-haemorrhages\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both; Each step in the management was discussed seperately. A detailed lecture was given on each step of management according to guidelines.For example-\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E1.A case of acute stroke in window period(\u0026lt;4.5hrs)-Clinical assessment,NIHSS score,BP control,GRBS,CT+\/-Angio, ASPECTS score, check list for thrombolysis, thrombolysis with alteplase, post thrombolysis monitoring, complications, and when to do repeat imaging were explained in detail by me.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E2.A wake up stroke-Detailed explanation about diffusion-flair mismatch was explained with the help of MRI images.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E3.A case of acute stroke outside the window period-Role of dual anti-platelet therapy and indications were discussed. Dosages of the drugs were discussed. Role of statins was discussed.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EFollowed by a brief lecture by me, on various scoring systems-\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ENIHSS score\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both; I hope eventually it becomes a habit and they incorporate this into their real-world clinical practice.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p1\" style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: auto; font-size: 17px; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal; margin: 0px; text-size-adjust: auto;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: inherit;\"\u003E___________________________________________________________________________-\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"color: #cc0000;\"\u003ECASE PRESENTATION-\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPresenter- Dr. Akash\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EModerator-Dr. Chandana\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThe session started with case presentation by Dr. Akash. The patient was a middle aged man with electric shock like pain sensation in trigeminal distribution ,each attack lasting 2-3mins , occurring several times a day. Patient also had conjunctival redness and lacrimation.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EDifferentials after the case presentation were,\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E-Trigeminal neuralgia\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E-Short lasting neuralgiform headaches\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EDr.Akash was assessed on his history taking skills for a \u0026nbsp;of headache\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EImportance of the following in case of headache was emphasised,\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E1.Age\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E2.Onset-\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EA case scenario of severe acute headache with sub-arachnoid haemorrhage was given as example.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E3.Region\/Location of headache\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EBilateral forehead-TTH\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EUnilateral, fronto-parietal-Migraine\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EUnilateral, orbital, supra-orbital, temporal-TACs\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EMaxillary, mandibular with or without ophthalmic division regions in trigeminal neuralgia.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E4.Radiation to neck-Meningitis\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E5.Characters of pain\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThrobbing, Pulsating-Migraine\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EDull, pressure like-TTH\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EStabbing-TACs\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EElectric shock like-Trigeminal neuralgia\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EWorst headache ever\/ thunderclap headache-SAH\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E6.Frequency in terms of how many times in a day? How many attacks in a month \/year?\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EHow much time is each attack lasting?\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E7.Red flag signs of headache were discussed\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E8.A example case scenario was given. Old aged male patient with proximal muscle weakness with temporal region pain and vision loss. Students identified it as GCA but failed to identify the associated polymyalgia rheumatica\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E9.Importance of other associated symptoms was discussed. Few of them are mentioned below,\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAura-Visual, Sensory, motor, retinal, speech, brain stem aura\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp;Photophobia, phonophobia, osmophobia (sensitivity to light, sounds, and movements respectively) are features of migraine.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ELimb weakness\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EVisual disturbance\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EFever, neck stiffness. photophobia, and rash suggest meningitis\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EScalp tenderness and jaw claudication are indicative of giant cell arteritis,\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ECranial autonomic symptoms were discussed\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EEar, tooth, facial, and neck pain are causes of referred pain to the head.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ENausea and vomiting are symptoms of migraine and elevated intracranial pressure.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EConstitutional symptoms: weight loss and anorexia suggesting. neoplastic disease, fever\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E10.Variour precipitants of headache\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E11. Aggrevating and relieving factors were discussed\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E12. Important questions to ask in family and personal history was explained in detail.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EStudents were explained about the importance of stress factors in headache. The students were advised to take history related to stress under 4 headings not to miss anything.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EWORK STRESS\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EFAMILY STRESS\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EFINANCIAL STRESS\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPSYCHOLOGICAL STRESS\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E13.Various medications and their relation to headache was discussed, for example,\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAnalgesics-Medication overuse headache\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ENitrates ,CCBs\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAnticoagulant,antiplatelets-ICH\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ESteroids, OCPs, Vitamin A, Tetracylines-IIH\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E14.Dr.Akash was questioned on the further evaluation and management.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EFurther discussion was on types of trigeminal neuralgias which are,\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EClassical TN-Due to vascular compression\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ESecondary TN-Due to Space occupying lesions, Demyelination etc with deficits in sensory and motor components of trigeminal nerve\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EIdiopathic TN-No cause.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E15.Importance of treatment resistant TN and MRI was discussed.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EMRI FIESTA sequence was a new term introduced to the students and they were encouraged to review the literature on this topic.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E16.Treatment was discussed as\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EFirst line drugs-Carbamazepine, oxcarbazepine along with dosages, side effects, and monitoring was discussed\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ESecond line drugs-Gabapentin,pregabalin, phenytoin\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EA brief discussion on alcohol block of mandibular and mental nerves followed by a discussion on Microvascular decompression in cases with vascular compression\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ERadiofrequency thermocoagulation in old age \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"color: #cc0000;\"\u003ESEMINAR \u003C\/span\u003EON SEIZURE SEMIOLOGY\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPresenter: Dr. HIMAJA\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EModerator: Dr. CHANDANA\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E18 post graduates attended the session\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ETo begin the discussion, postgraduates were asked if they can localize a seizure focus based on clinical history. Many post-graduates are unaware about seizure semiology and localization of seizure focus. They are always trained in stroke localization but seizure localization is something which is often overlooked and that needs a meticulous history taking.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThe discussion started with various signs and symptoms associated with seizures under the following headings:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E1.Aura\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E2.Automatisms\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E3.Motor manifestations such as posturing (figure of 4 posturing)\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E4.Eye manifestations: versive and non-versive eye movements\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E5.Language disturbances\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E6.Ictal and post ictal phenomenon\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EILAE 2017 classification of seizures was discussed and various changes that have been compared to previous ILAE classification were discussed\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EEach post-graduate was given a clinical scenario, where in the post-graduate tried localizing the seizure focus based on the semiology and they were assessed on their localizing skills.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAfter the exercise the discussion continued on,\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E1.Features of seizures with frontal lobe as a epileptogenic focus\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E2.Features of seizures with temporal lobe as a epileptogenic focus\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E3.Features of seizures with parietal lobe as a epileptogenic focus\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E4.Features of seizures with occipital lobe as a epileptogenic focus\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EGeneralized seizure semiology was discussed: GTCS,Generalized absence seizure,Generalized myoclonic seizure ,atonic seizure.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPost-session assessment with 10mcqs was conducted with main focus on lobar localization of seizure and ILAE 2017 classification of seizure.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ERESULTS:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EHighest 10\/10 highest 8\/10 👏\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EDr.Narsimha\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EDr.Deepika\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EDr.Hari \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"color: #cc0000;\"\u003ECASE PRESENTATION\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EBy Dr.Venkanna\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EA case each episode\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E2.Before the event:\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EProdromal symptoms\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPrecipitants\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAura\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAutomatisms\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E3.During the eveng\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ELoss of consciousness\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Elimb movements\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Eposturing\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Eeye and head movements\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Etongue bite, frothing, urine events\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E5.To rule out non epileptic attacks\/Psychological causes\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAtypical limb movements\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Eretained awareness during the event\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Evocalizations and response to commands during the attack\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Erapid recovery with\u0026nbsp; no post-ictal confusion\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Eatypical injuries\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThe discussion was followed by how to obtain relevant past medical history and drug NEURO-INFECTIONS\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPresenter: Dr. VIVEK\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EModerator: Dr. CHANDANA\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EDiscussion on\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E1.Meningitis\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E2.Brain abscess\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E3.Encephalitis\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E1.Meningitis\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EEach post-graduate was given a case of meningitis along with CSF findings to solve.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Ea. Bacterial meningitis\u0026nbsp; b. Viral meningitis c. Fungal meningitis\u0026nbsp; d. Tubercular meningitis\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThe post-graduates easily diagnosed bacterial meningitis but most of them got confused in differentiating viral meningitis and tubercular meningitis as both have lymphocyte predominance in CSF.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThis question solving exercise was followed by detailed discussion on the clinical presentation, CSF analysis and interpretation of CSF results to diagnose meningitis\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EDiscussion on management of each type of meningitis .\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EMany post-graduates seem to be unaware that enterovirus are the most common causative agent for viral meningitis and needs only supportive care rather than acyclovir. Indications of acyclovir in viral meningitis was explained in detail.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ECase scenario of HIV patient with meningitis was given and importance of having cryptococcal meningitis as differential was emphasized.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E2.Brain abscess\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EClinical presentation was discussed\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EMRI images were displayed and each post-graduate was asked to give one differential for ring enhancing lesion.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThis was followed by discussion on ring enhancing lesions\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EManagement of brain abscess was discussed.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E3. Encephalitis\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EHSV encephalitis, Dengue and COVID encephalitis was discussed briefly\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EDifferences between meningitis and encephalitis were discussed.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPOST-SEMINAR assessment results (10 mcqs)\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EHighest 9\/10\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EDr. Nagendra\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EDr. Vivek\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EDr. Narsimha\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EDr. Hari priya\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E2nd highest 8\/10\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EDr. Manohith\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EDr. Deepika\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EDr. Nishitha\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EDr. Venkat sai\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E3rd Highest 7\/10\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EDr. Ajay\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EDr. Lohith\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EDr. Shiva kumar\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EDr. Vyshnavi\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E_____________________________________________________________________\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"color: #cc0000;\"\u003ECASE PRESENTATION\u003C\/span\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EBy Dr. Ravi\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EMODERATOR: DR.CHANDANA\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ELink to the case report:\u0026nbsp;\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/drkeerthimadireddy.blogspot.com\/2024\/01\/60-m-tb-meningitis.html?m=1\"\u003E60 year male with HIV + TBM + Acute stroke\u003C\/a\u003E\u0026nbsp;+? Normal developmental milestones were achieved on time. Parents are first cousins, indicating a consanguineous marriage.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EPatient was thin, with mild generalized muscle atrophy. Bilateral\nptosis, worsened with sustained upward gaze. Mild facial\nweakness, especially in the orbicularis oculi and oris muscles.\nThe extraocular muscles showed mild weakness, but there was\nno significant ophthalmoplegia .Dropped jaw and bilateral\nflattening of the nasolabial folds. Normal Tone,Power:4\/5 in both\nlimbs. All Reflexes normal ,Gait normal but with mild fatigue on\nprolonged walking. Intact sensory system .Other specific tests like\nIce pack test and Simpson test are positive.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EDiscussion on diagnosis and management of congenital myaesthnia graves.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EPresentor: Dr. Vyshnavi\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EDiscussion by Dr.V.
